messages:
anna: Quick bakeoff drop — ran GPTQ profiles across Llama-2-70B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen-14B using our standard eval suite. TL;DR: GPTQ (4-bit, g128) keeps most instruction-following metrics for Llama and Mistral, Qwen shows a ~1.5-2.0% EM hit on long-context QA.

kai: Nice. Which families+configs did you compare? GPTQ only or AWQ/AWT/FP8 too?

anna: GPTQ 4-bit group128, GPTQ 3-bit group128 (aggressive), AWQ-4, and baseline FP16/FP32. Also a small INT8 path for Mistral where supported. Each run used the same quant seeds and conversion pipeline.

marco: Any weird failure modes? KV cache drift, decoding hangs, quant noise?

anna: Mostly stable. Notes: 
- Llama-2-70B: GPTQ-4 g128 = negligible instruction loss (avg ROUGE/ExactMatch delta ~ -0.6%). Latency improved ~2.8x vs FP16 on our A100 pool.
- Mistral-7B: GPTQ-4 g128 = ~-0.9% on instruction tasks but inference latency ~3.6x. AWQ-4 matched GPTQ for nll but had slightly worse multi-slot reasoning.
- Qwen-14B: GPTQ-4 g128 = ~-1.8% EM on long-context QA, and GPTQ-3 got another -2.5% hit. AWQ-4 was better for Qwen (only -1.1%).

sasha: Did you observe any tokenization/embedding regressions for Qwen specifically? We know Qwen's tokenizer can amplify quant noise for some rare tokens.

anna: Yes — rare-token generation degraded a bit in Qwen under GPTQ-3 and 4. Short warmup prefix caching reduces the effect — adding a 16-token prefix cache cut the rare-token reg rate in half in perf tests.

kai: Can you paste the short bench table (p50 latency, p95, throughput) for the three families on the default batch sizes?

anna: Sure — quick paste from bench harness (single A100-40GB, seq512, batch=1/4):
```
Model          | Config      | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | tokens/s
Llama-70B      | FP16        | 320     | 920     | 85
Llama-70B      | GPTQ-4 g128 | 110     | 360     | 240
Mistral-7B     | FP16        | 85      | 220     | 360
Mistral-7B     | GPTQ-4 g128 | 24      | 78      | 1250
Qwen-14B       | FP16        | 260     | 740     | 110
Qwen-14B       | GPTQ-4 g128 | 95      | 300     | 300
Qwen-14B       | AWQ-4       | 78      | 250     | 360
```

marco: Those Mistral gains are huge. Are we confident mixing GPTQ for Mistral and AWQ for Qwen in a single routing policy? Any KB/caching incompatibilities?

anna: We tested mixed routing — the runtime can pick quant backends per model variant. Requirements: model artifacts must include a backend tag and KV cache layout mapping. No cross-model cached kv reuse, obviously. We added a small shim so fallback rules prefer AWQ-4 for Qwen variants if GPTQ-runtime returns a decoding anomaly.

infra-bot: @team Note: for Dedicated pools, quantized models need the `quant_backend` flag set in model metadata to enable proper kernel selection. Missing flag => will serve as FP16 fallback.

kai: How about quality regression alerts? Any eval tasks spiking in hallucination or instruction compliance?

anna: Two callouts: Qwen GPTQ-4 shows a small hallucination uptick on multi-hop retrieval + long context (precision drop ~ -2.2% on our retrieval-exactness metric). Mistral stable across our instruction evals, but a tiny drop in math-chain reasoning for GPTQ-3. Overall we set threshold triggers: EM drop >1.5% or precision drop >2% => block promotion. By that rule, Qwen GPTQ-4 needs canary gated.

sasha: Did you run the calibration pass (per-channel scale updates) for GPTQ? Sometimes that recovers a lot.

anna: Yes — per-channel calibration and 512 batch calibration helped Qwen by ~0.6% EM. But not enough to reach baseline. We plan an extra pass with per-layer bias correction next.

marco: For deployment profiles, what's your recommendation for each family?

anna: Proposed defaults:
- Llama-70B: GPTQ-4 g128 for Dedicated; hosted -> GPTQ-4 with strict A/B canary and fallback to FP16.
- Mistral-7B: GPTQ-4 g128 for both hosted & dedicated (AWQ parity but GPTQ better latency in our kernels).
- Qwen-14B: AWQ-4 for hosted; keep FP16 option for sensitive customers; mark GPTQ-4 as experimental (must pass canary on customer-specific evals).

kai: Any config snippets to reproduce the quantization we used? Drop it here so infra can bake into CI.

anna: Pasting the quant command we used:
```
python tools/gptq/quantize.py --model-path models/<family>/<version> --out models-quant/<family>/gptq-4-g128 --bits 4 --group-size 128 --calib-batches 512 --per-channel --use-gpu
```

sasha: Thanks. Can you add the per-family eval CSVs to the artifacts bucket? I'll pick up detailed regression graphs.

anna: Will upload by EOD. For now I pushed a short artifact: s3://redwood-qa/gptq-bakes/1759999999/summary.json (contains metric deltas + canary pass flags).

eval-bot: Summary: Llama-70B[GPTQ-4]: PASS (canary), Mistral-7B[GPTQ-4]: PASS, Qwen-14B[AWQ-4]: RECOMMEND, Qwen-14B[GPTQ-4]: FAIL (canary) — see /evals/1759999999/ for full reports.

kai: Great work. Next steps: infra to add the metadata flag, eng-ml to re-run Qwen extended calibration, then schedule a canary for selected customers. I'll own the canary rollout plan. :thumbsup:

anna: Thanks — ping me if you want the raw logs. I noted a few HW-specific kernel slowdowns on older A100 gen1 machines; will include a per-cluster note in the upload.

marco: Awesome. small ask: add a one-liner in the model catalog entries about recommended quant backend and canary gate. saves confusion later.

anna: Will do. closing thread after uploads. :wave:
